facts.raw_span: asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area extending to the left eyebrow
lesions measured (length × width) 7 × 2 cm and 6 × 1 cm, respectively
Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
broken hairs were not seen
result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination shows predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis
Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
Antinuclear antibody: Negative
Antidouble-stranded DNA antibody: Negative

concepts.why: The patient's lesions show histopathologic features of lymphocytic infiltrates and hyaline fat necrosis, and direct immunofluorescence reveals granular deposition of immunoglobulins and complement, which are characteristic of discoid lupus erythematosus.
The patient's presentation of linear hair loss, alopecic patches, and dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs and honeycomb hyperpigmentation are consistent with lichen planopilaris.
The patient's pattern of hair loss, particularly the band-like alopecic lesion on the frontal scalp, is reminiscent of frontal fibrosing alopecia.

rationales.F01: The presence of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus and frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F02: Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning are common in lichen planopilaris and frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F05: Dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation are seen in discoid lupus erythematosus and lichen planopilaris.
rationales.F08: Histopathologic examination showing lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis is highly suggestive of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F09: Inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis are characteristic of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F10: Direct immunofluorescence positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels is typical of discoid lupus erythematosus.

frontier_selector.rationale: Histopathologic examination and direct immunofluorescence findings support Discoid lupus erythematosus, despite negative antinuclear and antidouble-stranded DNA antibodies.
